Notes: Best pick for a fixed bedside node: RP2350 (520KB RAM, TLS headroom) + hardwired W5500 TCP/IP Ethernet. Wired avoids hospital WiFi/RF restrictions and offloads the network stack from the MCU.
Use only if wired Ethernet is impossible. 2.4GHz WiFi (CYW43439). +1.00 with headers.
Only if you add networking separately. No use without an uplink.
~20-24, UNCONFIRMED (Amazon blocks automated price fetch). Bare SPI module - NOT the 40-pin HAT. SPI lines (CS/SCLK/MOSI/MISO/DRDY) wire directly to Pico GPIO. Matches the ADS1256 you already know.
This is the 40-pin HAT (the board you have). Can be wired to a Pico via jumpers but it is designed for a full Pi header - clumsy for a Pico build.

Product name: Precision RTC Module for Raspberry Pi Pico (DS3231)
Notes: Needed: RP2350 onboard RTC loses time on power-off. Battery-backed I2C clock for trustworthy timestamps when NTP is blocked. (Unlike the Pi 5, which has a battery-backed onboard RTC.)
For store-and-forward buffering during uplink outages (no Linux filesystem on a Pico). Use FAT with careful flush + the supercap (#7) to avoid corruption. Reuse a 32GB A2 card.
Only 2 channels - enough for one-direction UART / a couple of digital lines, NOT a full SPI bus. For a patient-connected RS-232 instrument see the ADM3251E note below.
TTL UART <-> RS-232. NOT isolated. Pair with #5, or replace both with an isolated transceiver (ADM3251E, 2.5kV, isoPower) for a true patient-safe barrier - bare IC only, custom board needed.

column10: Powers the node over the same Ethernet run (802.3af -> 5V). Isolated. Cleaner than a separate PSU for a wired bedside node.

Notes: No off-the-shelf Pico-scale module at Pi Hut/Pimoroni. ~5 estimate for a supercap. Gives enough hold-up to flush the SD buffer on power loss. A Pico needs far less of a UPS than a Pi - it resets cleanly, no OS to corrupt.
